disposition_mapping.rationale: The council converged on separating mechanical cadence/timetable/template mechanics (automatable) from the curatorial judgment of deciding which macro items and business events actually matter this cycle (human, per hitl_designer and finance_domain). The FP&A manager remains the named accountable author of the assumptions pack rather than a rubber-stamp reviewer of a fully autonomous draft, addressing agentic_architect's own caution against letting the manager step back from per-cycle review. Multi-channel distribution addresses emerging_economy's non-negotiable on infrastructure parity.

Extraction and mapping mechanics are automated per the near-unanimous view that this is the strongest mechanization candidate, but the council rejected (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) collapsing the cutoff/completeness check into a checkpoint-free pipeline. KB-03's reporting-period discipline is preserved as a hard, structural gate with a named accountable reviewer for exceptions, and the step is kept distinct rather than merged into RF-01 or RF-03, following the majority view favouring separately observable ingestion for failure-isolation reasons.

The mechanical/judgment fault line already present in RF-03's description is made architectural: FX and run-rate refresh is automated with exchange differences kept separately visible per KB-08 (a live requirement per accounting_standards and finance_domain), while pricing, volume and headcount judgment remain human-entered and are now explicitly tagged by source, per hitl_designer's and finance_domain's converging design (adopted as a governance mechanism, not an IAS 8 mandate, per accounting_standards' correction). Kept as its own step rather than folded into RF-01 or RF-02, consistent with the majority position.

The council decisively rejected maximalist's AI-drafted-with-attestation model: pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer and agentic_architect independently converged that BU finance leads must originate the substantive forecast assertion because constructing and defending a number is a different accountability act from attesting to a machine's draft, and because this is the one channel structurally capable of capturing information a model cannot see. The function is restructured, not merely retained, by embedding real-time validation at the point of submission (agentic_architect's refinement, accepted by hitl_designer and finance_domain), absorbing part of RF-05's function forward to eliminate rework round-trips.

The validation function is split rather than eliminated or fully automated into a single engine: BU-level completeness and coherence checks move forward into TS-04 for immediate feedback, while genuinely group-level checks (intercompany, cross-entity FX consistency, aggregate continuity) - invisible until submissions are aggregated - remain a distinct step (TS-05) under an accountable analyst, per agentic_architect's architecture and finance_domain's and pragmatist's insistence that a chase-and-correct exception path stay named and visible. FPA-R-02 is satisfied explicitly: TS-05 continues to consume the closed-period actuals baseline as a structural input. Any consolidation methodology change must be surfaced, not silently coded in, per accounting_standards' KB-06 hold.

The council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) rejected maximalist's merger of variance analysis into the same engine as consolidation validation, on the grounds that validation and interpretation are different failure classes whose collapse risks an analyst narrating a data error as a trend. Variance analysis is preserved per FPA-R-01 as its own step: bridge arithmetic is machine-computed, but the interpretive narrative remains human-authored from the decomposition, not edited from a machine draft, per hitl_designer's distinction between authored and reviewed content.

Universally protected as a non-delegable human governance gate (FPA-R-03; every council member's non-negotiables). The council converged, following hitl_designer's and agentic_architect's refinement (conceded by maximalist), that the gate must receive full traceability - the tagged assumption log, the exception log, and the bridge plus human narrative - rather than a single rolled-up figure, to prevent the ceremonial-approval failure mode identified across multiple positions.

Publication survives per FPA-R-05 and is sequenced strictly after approval per FPA-R-04, now enforced as a technical precondition (a verified approval token/authorization) rather than only a process convention, per agentic_architect's design, adopted by the council. Mechanical distribution and archiving are automated, but hitl_designer's and agentic_architect's converged refinement adds a named accountable release-check confirming published content matches the approved version, closing the evidential gap between approval and what stakeholders actually receive. Low-bandwidth/offline fallback for distribution and archiving addresses emerging_economy's and pragmatist's non-negotiable.

steps.description: A calendar-triggered system drafts the assumptions pack from macro-indicator and corporate-target feeds and prepares the timetable and templates automatically. The FP&A manager remains the visible, accountable author of the assumptions pack: reviewing the system-drafted content, adding or editing judgment items (known business events, corporate-target changes) that a feed cannot originate, and approving distribution. Timetable and templates are distributed through both live-system and low-bandwidth/offline channels (email, static file, shared drive) so business units without reliable portal access are not excluded.
steps.name: Cycle initiation and assumptions curation

steps.description: GL and management-reporting extraction and structural mapping run as an automated, scheduled feed. A hard period-lock/cutoff check must pass before any extract is treated as a validated baseline, preserving reporting-period discipline (KB-03) even where mechanics are automated. Exceptions such as mapping breaks, late postings, restatements, and incomplete extracts are not auto-resolved; they are routed to a named accountable FP&A analyst for review and correction. The load is versioned and reversible so any baseline can be reconstructed or rolled back. Where a business unit's data arrives via a manual/offline channel, the same cutoff gate applies before that data enters the baseline.
steps.name: Automated actuals ingestion with cutoff-gated exception review
outputs: closed-period actuals (validated baseline) loaded to forecast model

steps.description: Mechanically refreshed drivers (FX rates, actual run-rates) are auto-refreshed from source feeds, with exchange-rate effects kept as a separately identifiable, traceable component rather than netted into a blended growth or cost figure (KB-08). Judgment-based drivers (pricing, volume/demand calls, headcount and cost-inflation assumptions) are entered or explicitly overridden by an identifiable human working with business/operations input, and every driver value is tagged as system-sourced or judgment-sourced (with attribution) so downstream reviewers can distinguish the two. Missing judgment input triggers a time-bound, SLA-governed escalation to the FP&A analyst or manager rather than a silent default.
steps.name: Driver assumption refresh - mechanical and judgment tracks
outputs: Updated driver assumptions (tagged: system-sourced vs judgment-sourced)

steps.description: BU finance leads originate their own revenue, cost, headcount and capex projections and commentary explaining changes since the prior forecast - this remains a substantively human-authored assertion, not a machine-generated draft awaiting attestation, because it is the workflow's primary channel for information no model can see. A validation function embedded at the point of submission gives BU leads real-time feedback on completeness, headcount-to-cost coherence and continuity against actuals, replacing the prior downstream discovery-and-chase cycle for the majority of anomalies. Submission remains possible through offline/spreadsheet channels where live system integration is unavailable.
steps.name: BU forecast submission with embedded validation

steps.description: BU submissions are aggregated automatically into the group forecast model. Group-level checks that are only observable once submissions are combined - intercompany coherence, cross-entity FX consistency, aggregate continuity against actuals - run automatically, and this step continues to consume the closed-period actuals baseline directly as a structural input, not a reference document. Flagged exceptions are resolved or escalated by a named accountable FP&A analyst via an explicit, SLA-bound chase-and-correct loop back to TS-04 rather than an undocumented side channel. Any change to consolidation methodology (new engine, changed matching or aggregation logic) is surfaced as a disclosed methodology change, not silently absorbed into an automated system update, preserving policy consistency (KB-06).
steps.name: Group-level consolidation and validation

steps.description: Bridge and waterfall arithmetic and driver/business-unit decomposition against budget and prior forecast are machine-computed directly from the validated consolidated model. The risk/opportunity narrative and interpretive judgment - why a movement occurred, whether it is structural or one-off, what range of outcomes it implies - remain human-authored by the FP&A analyst working from the machine-built decomposition, not edited from a machine-drafted explanation. This step remains distinct from consolidation validation because it answers a different question (what the data means, not whether the data is right), and collapsing the two risks an analyst narrating a movement that is actually a data error.
steps.name: Variance analysis

steps.description: The CFO/FP&A director conducts a real challenge session fed by full traceability rather than a single rolled-up figure: the driver assumption log distinguishing system-sourced from judgment-sourced entries (TS-03), the group-level exception log (TS-05), and the machine-built bridge together with its human-authored narrative (TS-06). Directed revisions may loop back to TS-03, TS-04, TS-05 or TS-06 for re-work, not merely a re-stamp. Approval, once given, issues a verifiable, logged authorization that governs downstream publication.
steps.name: Management review and approval

steps.description: Publication mechanics - updating planning systems, distributing the forecast pack and commentary, archiving the version with its assumptions log - are automated, but execution is hard-gated: the publication function must verify a signed, logged approval authorization from TS-07 before it fires, enforcing approval-before-publication as a technical precondition rather than a process convention. A named accountable FP&A manager performs a release check confirming that what is published is bit-for-bit the version that was approved, closing the loop against last-mile edits. Distribution and archiving support low-bandwidth/offline fallback (batch export/import, locally-held archive copy) alongside any live system update.
steps.name: Publish forecast and reporting
